title: A replay turns the whole page into a non-interactive dead zone for ~15s, with no visible escape once the visitor scrolls
evidence: R4.1 calls setChromeInert(sectionRef.current, true) in handleReplay (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-re3zy/b1a3eebd-71bd-4681-8fbe-fedeec4d6c0a/scratchpad/gcl/apps/gabriel-capital-labs-site/components/ArrivalScene.tsx:958) and adds html.gcl-replaying, which hides the nav — but a replay never re-applies the scroll lock, so the page stays scrollable while everything on it is inert. Measured 1440x900 full-motion: a mid-replay 5-press Tab sweep cycles only [A.skip-link, BUTTON.arrival__replay] with 8 [inert] elements; the CONTROL under identical input reaches A.ecosystem__wing-link, BUTTON.footer__link, A.footer__link. A real mouse wheel(0,3000) mid-replay gives: navOpacity 0 / visibility hidden, inertCount 8, and .arrival__skip (position:absolute per globals.css:715, not fixed) at top=-2973 with skipOnScreen=false — the visitor sees a scrollable page with no nav, no skip chip and nothing clickable. Measured 7,647ms still to run before inert was released in that sample (up to ~15s from the click). CONTROL at the same moment: navOpacity 1, inertCount 0, fully interactive. Esc does rescue it (verified: inert=0, nav visible after Esc), but the replay announcement is "Replaying introduction" — unlike the first-visit announcement it never mentions Escape. Not present in the control, and not present in pre-remediation R4.
fix: The containment is only needed while overflow:hidden already makes the rest of the page unreachable. Scope setChromeInert(true) to the first-visit prologue branch and drop it from handleReplay (keep html.gcl-replaying for the visual nav withhold). If containment on replay is genuinely wanted, make .arrival__skip position:fixed for the replay window and add the Escape affordance to the replay announcement. Regression test: mid-replay wheel(0,3000), then assert at least one focusable page element and a non-zero elementsFromPoint hit outside the arrival section.

title: The gold REPLAY ARRIVAL chip is left at full opacity through every replay's P1 and is the brightest element on screen
evidence: Measured at replay t=4.8s (P2 peak), 1440x900 full-motion, after a completed first play: the chip's brightest pixel is RGB(212,161,70) — pure --gcl-gateway-gold at opacity 1 — against the P2 gold signal's RGB(120,91,42) and the newly dimmed SKIP chip's RGB(121,121,122). Relative luminance 0.399 vs 0.116: the chip is 3.4x the phase's hero element, in the same brand colour. Screenshot at replay t=2400ms (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-re3zy/b1a3eebd-71bd-4681-8fbe-fedeec4d6c0a/scratchpad/r4f/shots/replay-full-2400.png) shows a frame whose only content is that gold-bordered chip bottom-left, during the phase specified as "Darkness. Silence. No UI, no nav, no text." Probe across 3 consecutive replays: rep=1.0000/visible at t=200/1400/2400/4800/9000ms every time. Cause: setShowReplay(false) is still gated behind !isDesktopWidthNow (ArrivalScene.tsx:908), so a desktop replay never hides it, and html.gcl-replaying (globals.css:281) covers .nav only. The original finding named this chip explicitly alongside the nav and the SKIP chip; the other two were fixed and this one was not, so finding 4(b) is not resolved.
fix: Extend the html.gcl-replaying rule to .arrival__replay as a visual-only hide (opacity/visibility, leaving the element in the DOM so R3.1 Finding 16's aria-busy/AX presence during replay is preserved), or dim it to the same restrained target revealSkip now uses for the SKIP chip. Re-measure the chip's brightest pixel at replay t=2400ms and assert it is at or below the P2 signal.

title: After a mid-prologue 1024px crossing the Gateway G renders at 104% scale for the rest of the session
evidence: R4 at 1440x900 full-motion, setViewportSize(390x844) at t=3.0s. Measured .arrival__mark-wrap computed transform matrix(1.04, 0, 0, 1.04, 0, 0), box 124.8x135.2 at y=284.81 — stable at +500ms, +3s and +8s. A NATIVE 390 load is matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0), 120x130 at y=287.41. The oversize carries into the mobile pull-back: at scrollY=300 the crossed mark scrubs to scale 0.957 vs the control's 0.9407. CONTROL is exact at every sample (crossed == native == 120x130, matrix(1,...)). Whole-viewport pixel diff crossed-390 vs native-390: 3,827 px (1.16%), bbox (25,28)-(228,771), maxDelta 230. Mechanism: globals.css:592 sets the desktop pre-hidden state `html.js .arrival__mark-wrap { transform: translateY(18px) scale(1.04) }`; when the query flips, gsap.matchMedia rebuilds pinCtx and the newly created mobile pull-back tween `.to(markWrapRef.current, { scale: 0.9 })` (ArrivalScene.tsx:731) captures the mark's then-current 1.04 as its start before handleBreakpointChange's tl.progress(1,false) lands, so y returns to 0 but scale never returns to 1. The handler's own comment claims "nothing prologue-only leaks into the mobile composition the visitor now sees" — this falsifies it. Same run, secondary: the handler's gsap.set(skipButtonRef.current,{clearProps:'all'}) does not stick — inline style after the crossing is "pointer-events: auto; opacity: 0.65; visibility: inherit;" vs "" on a native 390 load, because revealSkip's 0.4s tween is fired by the same progress(1,false) and re-writes after the clear (no visual consequence: the element is hidden/display:none by then).
fix: After the abort, re-assert the composed transform on the next frame — requestAnimationFrame(() => gsap.set(markWrapRef.current, { y: 0, scale: 1 })) — and re-arm the newly built mobile trigger with ScrollTrigger.refresh() so it captures scale 1 as its scrub start. Move the skip-chip clearProps into the same rAF (or kill the revealSkip tween first). Regression test: cross at t=3.0s, then assert getComputedStyle(markWrap).transform === 'matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)' and a zero pixel diff against a native 390 load.

title: The mobile tagline is repaired at 320-375 but untouched at 393-430, where it becomes the widest element in the composition
evidence: Measured R4 vs control at full composition. text-wrap: balance is supported here (CSS.supports true, computed 'balance') and does fix 320: two lines of 182.3 / 149.1px, replacing the reported 278+53 orphan. Identical at 360 and 375 (182.3 / 149.1) — both narrower than the 209.3px GABRIEL wordmark, so the centred pyramid holds. From 393 up the line fits on one row at 335.7px: 85% of a 393 viewport, 81% at 412 and 414, 78% at 430 — and 1.6x the wordmark, so the tagline becomes the widest element and inverts the arrival's hierarchy. Control is 232.6px on one line at every one of those widths. balance is inert wherever the text already fits, so the prescribed fix's second half ("pull 390px back off the gutters") never landed. Net effect: the iPhone SE / 13-mini / Galaxy S class (360-375) and the iPhone 14-16 / Pixel class (393-430) now render materially different arrival compositions. Everything else on mobile is clean and I confirm it independently: pins 2/2 (no-preference) and 0/0 (reduce), document heights byte-identical at all six width/policy combos (320: 10165 and 7592; 390: 9631 and 7059; 768: 9785 and 7617), glow and cue boxes dx=dy=dw=0, atmosphere and signal computed 0 at every mobile combination, inline-style counts differing by exactly 1.
fix: Give .arrival__tagline-line a max-width below 1024px (around 20rem) so every phone width resolves to the same balanced two-line block inside the wordmark measure, then re-measure the per-width line counts. Alternatively, Founder accepts the 360/375-vs-393+ split as-is — but it should be an explicit decision, not a side effect of balance being inert.

title: The 18s dead-man watchdog's safety margin was silently spent by the P4 hold extension
evidence: Both watchdogs fire at 18,000ms from the pre-paint script (app/layout.tsx:130 setTimeout, globals.css:463 gcl-prologue-watchdog keyframe). Independently verified: with **/_next/static/chunks/main-app-*.js aborted the lock released at 18,241ms and the page then scrolled to 1500; with the page chunk aborted, 18,207ms; with window.setTimeout neutered before load AND all chunks aborted, animationName reported gcl-prologue-watchdog and overflow flipped to visible at 18,229ms — so both mechanisms are real and independent. Meanwhile finding 13's +0.7s hold extension moved the prologue's own completion to a measured 15,142ms (1024px) / 15,137ms (1920px), and the gap keeps closing under load: unlock 13,806ms at 1x CPU, 14,144ms at 4x, 14,340ms at 6x, and 14,540ms at 6x CPU + 400ms chunk delay, with completion at 16,126ms in that worst case. Margin between the prologue finishing and the watchdog firing is now roughly 2.1s in the slowest configuration I measured, down from about 4.2s unthrottled. I did NOT reproduce an actual preemption in any run — this is a margin finding, not an observed failure. If hydration ever exceeds it, the watchdog releases the lock mid-P5 and the pull-back scrub can fight the prologue's own glow/mark writes, with reclaimPrologueGlow no longer able to intervene (awaken unregisters it and completedRef guards it).
fix: Derive the watchdog from the prologue's real budget plus headroom (25s rather than 18s), or have the mount effect cancel and reschedule it once React owns the lock — and add a comment tying the constant to the timeline's total duration so a future beat-table change cannot silently eat the margin again.

title: A new infinite CSS animation runs under prefers-reduced-motion, justified by a precedent that is actually in the freeze list
evidence: globals.css:890 sets `.arrival--awake .arrival__atmosphere { animation: gcl-atmosphere-breathe 9s ease-in-out infinite alternate }`. Measured at 1440x900 with reducedMotion 'reduce': animationName gcl-atmosphere-breathe, duration 9s, iteration-count infinite, computed opacity oscillating 0.0720 to 0.0987 (delta 0.0267) — identical to the no-preference run. The control has no such animation (animationName null, opacity flat 0). The in-file comment justifies omitting it from the reduce guard as the "same precedent as `.arrival--static .arrival__glow` above" — but that selector IS inside the @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) freeze block near globals.css:126, and measured, its animationName is 'none' with zero movement in both builds and both policies. So the cited precedent points the opposite way. Practical impact is nil: the gradient is rgba(212,161,70,0.05), and the entire breathe moves the centre pixel by well under 1/255 (measured max 9 against a background of 8), so this is a correctness-of-record issue rather than a vestibular one.
fix: Either add `.arrival--awake .arrival__atmosphere` to the reduce guard's selector list — which the file itself documents as "meant to be exhaustive, not representative" — or rewrite the comment to state plainly that this is a deliberate exception to that list, not an application of it, so the next reader does not trust a false precedent.

title: "Skip to content" is a dead control for the prologue's 13.5s, and Enter on the SKIP chip still drops focus to <body>
evidence: At t=1.5s on R4, Tab then Enter on the skip-link sets location.hash='#content' but leaves scrollY=0 with gcl-prologue still applied and document.activeElement on BODY; the next three Tabs cycle skip-link, BODY, skip-link — so the standard bypass-block affordance does nothing for the duration of the lock. The containment itself is otherwise exactly right and is a clear improvement: an 8-press Tab sweep at t=3.6s stays inside {A.skip-link, BUTTON.arrival__skip} with scrollY 0 and nav opacity 0 at every press, where the control escapes to scrollY 6214 then 12232 with nav rising to 1. Separately, activating the SKIP chip with Enter lands focus on BODY — measured identically in R4 and in the control, so inherited rather than an R4 regression, but finding 12's prescribed second half (headingRef.current?.focus({preventScroll:true}) before hiding the chip) was not implemented, and under R4 that chip is a mandated, load-bearing affordance rather than a decoration. Working bypasses do exist and all resolve correctly: SKIP visible and focusable at 3.07s, Esc at any time, both announced, and every skip path (Esc at 1.2/3.6/9.0s, mouse click, keyboard Enter, both policies) lands on the same fully composed state with inert released and "Introduction complete" spoken.
fix: Either make the skip-link's activation abort the prologue while the lock is applied (a focusin/click handler on it calling timelineRef.current.progress(1,false), the same escape path Esc uses), or give #content tabindex=-1 so the jump at least moves focus. Separately, move focus to headingRef before markComplete sets hidden on the SKIP chip, reusing the R3.1 Finding 16 pattern already applied to the replay chip.

title: Replay now removes the whole page from focus and hit-testing for 13.4s while scroll stays unlocked — a scrolled visitor gets a dead page with no visible escape
evidence: The R4.1 F4 fix calls `setChromeInert(sectionRef.current, true)` in handleReplay (ArrivalScene.tsx:957) and adds `html.gcl-replaying` (globals.css hides `.nav` with `opacity/visibility/pointer-events !important`), but a replay deliberately does NOT re-apply the scroll lock. Measured on the R4 build, 1440x900, full motion, after one complete first play: inert count is 8 (HEADER.nav + SECTION.institution/mission/ecosystem/lab/principles/engagement + FOOTER.footer) for 13,385ms from the replay click until awaken() clears it. Mid-replay I scrolled to scrollY 5000 and sampled: nav computed opacity 0 with visibility hidden, inert still 8, and `document.querySelector('main > section:not(.arrival) a').closest('[inert]')` returns truthy — elementsFromPoint over the ecosystem wing link returns MAIN, not the link. The mandated skip affordance is unreachable at that scroll position: `.arrival__skip` is position:absolute and measured at top:-4973, i.e. 4973px above the viewport. Escape does recover cleanly (inert 0, nav opacity 1, gcl-replaying cleared) but the live region reads only "Replaying introduction" for the entire duration — the Escape hint exists only in the first-visit announcement. CONTROL under the identical replay-then-scroll sequence: inert 0, no inert ancestor on the same link, nav opacity 1 / visibility visible — fully interactive throughout. This is a regression the remediation introduced; it exists in neither the control nor pre-remediation R4.
fix: A replay must not contain focus it has not also contained scroll for. Either (a) drop `setChromeInert` from handleReplay entirely and rely on `gcl-replaying` + the z-index:700 chip for the visual withhold (the click-hijack half of F4 is already fixed by z-index alone — I verified the chip is first in elementsFromPoint at z 700 against the nav's 600), or (b) release inert the moment the visitor scrolls during a replay: add a one-shot `scroll` listener while `gcl-replaying` is set that calls `setChromeInert(section,false)` and removes the class. If inert is kept, also make the chip `position:fixed` for the replay duration and add "press Escape to skip" to the replay announcement. Regression test: start a replay, scroll 5000px, assert `closest('[inert]')` is null on a section link and that a nav link is hit-testable.

title: The two hydration dead-man watchdogs release the scroll lock but not the `inert` containment — a slow load yields a scrollable page where nothing outside the arrival responds
evidence: The F0 fix arms two 18s watchdogs (inline `setTimeout` in layout.tsx and the `gcl-prologue-watchdog` keyframe in globals.css) that both only do `classList.remove('gcl-prologue')` / flip `overflow`. Neither touches the `inert` attributes that the F2/F6 fix applies at mount, which are cleared exclusively inside `awaken()` at timeline position 13.1 (+0.4s delay). The watchdogs start at pre-paint; the timeline starts after hydration — so any load where hydration lands more than ~4.5s after pre-paint opens a window. Reproduced twice on the R4 build at 1440x900: (a) route-delaying `**/_next/static/chunks/**` by 6000ms — overflow flips to visible at 18,568ms with inert still 8 and the tagline still at opacity 0, inert not cleared until 19,974ms: a 1,406ms window; (b) a realistic profile, CDP `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` 6x plus Slow-3G (400kbps/400ms RTT) — inert applied at 13,520ms, lock released by the watchdog at 23,094ms, inert cleared at 26,635ms: a 3,541ms window, sampled every 500ms with `overflow:'visible', lock:false, inert:8, tag:'0'` at 23.09/23.60/24.10/24.61/25.11/25.61/26.12s. In that window the visitor can scroll (the lock is gone) into content where the nav, all six non-arrival sections and the footer are removed from the tab order and from hit-testing.
fix: Make the release atomic. Give `setChromeInert` its own dead-man: in the same inline script that arms the 18s `setTimeout`, also strip `[inert]` (`document.querySelectorAll('[inert]').forEach(e=>e.removeAttribute('inert'))`), and/or have the component register a `transitionend`/timer that calls `setChromeInert(section,false)` whenever `html.gcl-prologue` is observed to have been removed by something other than awaken() (a MutationObserver on documentElement.classList is the cheapest reliable hook). Regression test: delay the chunk route by 6000ms and assert `document.querySelectorAll('[inert]').length === 0` at the instant `overflow` becomes visible.

title: The crossing abort still leaks into the mobile composition: the Gateway G is left permanently at 104%, plus a breathing atmosphere and a stale skip-chip inline style a native mobile load never has
evidence: handleBreakpointChange (ArrivalScene.tsx:573) runs `tl.progress(1,false)` then `gsap.set([atmosphere,signal],{clearProps:'all'})` and `gsap.set(skip,{clearProps:'all'})`. Three leaks survive, all measured at scrollY 0, seven seconds after the crossing, against a native 390x844 load of the SAME build. (1) MARK SCALE: `.arrival__mark-wrap` carries inline `transform: translate3d(0px,0px,0px) scale(1.04,1.04)` and `img.arrival__mark` measures 124.8x135.2 instead of the native 120x130 — exactly +4%. Deterministic: 2/2 repetitions at each of t=1500ms, 3000ms and 6000ms (six for six). Clean at t=9000ms and t=12000ms, i.e. it leaks whenever the crossing precedes the P3 markWrap settle. CONTROL measures 120x130 in all ten equivalent runs. The mobile pull-back's own `markWrap` recede then scrubs from 104% instead of 100%. (2) ATMOSPHERE: `.arrival` retains `arrival--awake` after every crossing, so `.arrival--awake .arrival__atmosphere{animation:gcl-atmosphere-breathe}` keeps running — computed opacity 0.0951/0.0947/0.098 across runs, against exactly 0 on a native mobile load, in all five crossing times tested. (3) SKIP CHIP: `.arrival__skip` retains inline `pointer-events: auto; opacity: 0.65; visibility: inherit;` because revealSkip()'s 0.4s tween is started by the same `progress(1)` call and writes AFTER the clearProps runs — it is display:none via the `hidden` attribute so it is not visible, but it is an inline-style leak the R3 mobile gate forbids. Structurally the abort is otherwise clean: docH 9345/7003 and pin counts 2/0 match native exactly. Real trigger: iPad Pro 11" (1194/834) and iPad Air (1180/820) both cross 1024px on rotation during the ~15s prologue.
fix: Order the cleanup after the timeline has actually settled and include markWrap: replace the immediate `gsap.set(...clearProps)` with a `requestAnimationFrame`-deferred (or `tl.eventCallback('onComplete')`-chained) clear that also covers `markWrapRef` and kills any in-flight revealSkip tween (`gsap.killTweensOf(skipButtonRef.current)` before the clear). Clear `arrival--awake` on a crossing abort (`setAwake(false)` inside handleBreakpointChange) so the atmosphere returns to its rest 0 on the mobile composition. Regression test: cross at t=1500/3000/6000 and assert `img.arrival__mark` measures 120x130 and `.arrival__atmosphere` computes 0, both matching a native 390px load.

title: The F15 pathname gate desynchronised the two predicates: on /index.html the lock is correctly absent but the prologue still applies `inert` for 13.1s over an unlocked, scrollable page
evidence: layout.tsx now gates the pre-paint script on `location.pathname === '/'`, but ArrivalScene's `willRunPrologue` (line 221) still checks only width, hash and session — the code's own comment demands the two stay "a literal twin". Measured on R4 at http://127.0.0.1:4310/index.html, 1440x900, sampled every second: `html` never gains `gcl-prologue`, `overflow` is `visible` throughout, yet `document.querySelectorAll('[inert]').length` is 8 from 196ms to 13,274ms and only reaches 0 at 14,278ms. The skip chip reads `visibility: visible` from the very first sample (the `html.gcl-prologue .arrival__skip` CSS gate is what normally withholds it), so P1's "no UI" is broken on that route too, and the nav rises to opacity 1 at 14.3s. CONTROL at /index.html: inert 0. /404.html and an unknown /nope path are both correct on R4 and identical to control (no class, overflow visible, inert 0) — the 404 half of F15 is genuinely fixed. Reachability is deployment-dependent (Vercel may 308 /index.html to /), but the divergence is structural and any future route inherits it.
fix: Put the pathname check on the same side of the predicate as everything else: add `window.location.pathname === '/'` to `willRunPrologue` in ArrivalScene.tsx so the component and the pre-paint script agree, or better, export one shared predicate string and interpolate it into both. Regression test: load /index.html and assert `[inert].length === 0` at every sample.

title: The SKIP chip is still the brightest element in P2 — dimmed as prescribed, but the goal of letting the gold signal lead was not reached, and the contrast margin is now thin
evidence: revealSkip's resting target is 0.65 (verified: computed opacity 0.65 at P2, 1 on :hover, back to 0.65 on unhover, 1 on :focus-visible). Raw pixel measurement of the P2 frame at t=4.8s, 1440x900: the chip's brightest pixel is RGB(121,121,122) (relative luminance 121) while the gold signal's brightest pixel is RGB(120,91,42) (luminance ~94). The chip is therefore still ~29% brighter than the phase's hero element, and still a cool neutral in an obsidian-and-gold scene — improved from the measured 183 vs 119 but not resolved. Computed contrast of RGB(121,121,122) against the measured background RGB(6,6,8) is 4.655:1 — above the 4.5:1 AA floor but with almost no headroom, and axe-core 4.10 (wcag2a/2aa/21a/21aa/best-practice) reports 0 violations at 2s, 6s, 11s and 17s in both policies, so nothing would catch a future drift below the line.
fix: Optional craft call. If the Founder wants P2's signal to lead, give the chip a prologue-scoped gold treatment (`html.gcl-prologue .arrival__skip{color:var(--gcl-gateway-gold);border-color:rgba(212,161,70,.35)}`) at the same 0.65, which lands it inside the palette and below the signal in perceived luminance while keeping AA. Either way, record 4.655:1 as the measured floor so a later dimming is caught.

title: The site's own "Skip to content" link is a dead end for the whole prologue and leaves a hash in the URL
evidence: Measured on R4 at t=1.5s (P1), 1440x900: Tab once to A.skip-link, press Enter. Result: URL becomes http://127.0.0.1:4310/#content, scrollY stays 0 (the lock correctly holds), `document.activeElement` is BODY, inert count still 8. The three subsequent Tab presses land on BODY, A.skip-link, A.skip-link — the visitor never reaches the arrival skip chip from there and the skip-link accomplishes nothing. `<main id="content">` is not itself inert (only its children are) but has no tabindex, so focus falls to body. Side effect: the `#content` hash now in the URL means a reload takes the hash-bypass branch and silently skips the prologue.
fix: Either point the skip-link at the arrival skip chip while `html.gcl-prologue` is set, or give `<main id="content">` `tabIndex={-1}` so the link lands somewhere real and the next Tab reaches the chip. Cheap and self-contained.

title: On a slow device the prologue overruns the Founder's 12-16s window — a hydration-latency effect, not a beat-table one
evidence: At native speed the sequence is comfortably inside the window: awaken() fires at 13,581ms and the live region resolves to "Introduction complete" at 15,185ms from navigation (P4 hold measured at 3,123ms: last movement 7,946ms, first word beat 11,069ms). Under CDP CPU throttling 4x plus Regular-3G, the same build released the lock and cleared inert at 17,838ms from navigation, with the tagline only reaching opacity 1 at 17,336ms. Under 6x plus Slow-3G it ran to 26,635ms. The beat table itself is correct; the overrun is entirely the gap between pre-paint and hydration.
fix: No code change required if the window is understood as measured from prologue start rather than from navigation. If it is meant from navigation, shorten the outer delay or start the timeline from the pre-paint timestamp (`performance.timing`-anchored seek) so a slow hydration compresses the prologue rather than delaying it.
